transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-07 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ruth Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (CTO - VanguardAI), Daniel Kwan (SRE Lead), Lina Morales (Security)

Summary:
Quick status check on private pilot stability. Focus on MTU/fragmentation causing intermittent tail latency spikes, kernel offload tuning, KV cache cold starts after failover, and telemetry sampling cadence. Agreement to run synthetic fragmentation tests and share traces; kernel tuning playbook to be circulated.

Topics:
- MTU & IPsec fragmentation
- NIC offload and sysctl kernel tuning
- KV cache warmup / prefix caching behavior
- Telemetry sampling & golden trace selection
- Next-step bakeoff schedule and compliance doc requests

Transcript:
[00:00] Ruth Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um we'll do a quick 50-ish minute sync. Miguel and I will cover the infra changes we pushed last week and go through the results you shared.
[00:28] Priya Shah: sounds good, thanks Ruth. we had some noisy p99s last thursday during the sim, so we'd like to understand the fragmentation hypothesis.
[00:45] Miguel Alvarez: yeah, so quick context — last week we enabled IPsec tunnel between your colo and the private cluster and bumped the MTU to 1450. we noticed some reassembly on packets when jumbo frames are involved and that correlated with 99th percentile spikes.
[01:12] Daniel Kwan: yeah that matches our tcpdump — we saw lots of DF=1 fragments and then retransmits. also, on failover sequences the KV cache seems cold for longer than expected, maybe because of prefix invalidation.
[01:40] Miguel Alvarez: right, the runtime's prefix/K-V cache expiry defaults to 60s in this pilot image, and with the kinetic traffic patterns your cold-starts are visible. two things: we can tweak the cache TTL and also pre-warm via synthetic prefix hits during cutover.
[02:05] Lina Morales: quick sec — from security pov we need to ensure the IPsec settings align with our compliance, esp AES-GCM and key rotation windows. we also need audit logs for key usage.
[02:28] Ruth Chen: noted Lina, we'll include KMS rotation notes. Miguel, can you talk about NIC offload settings? we saw you changed GRO/TSO last patch.
[02:40] Miguel Alvarez: yeah sure — we disabled GRO on the host nic to reduce large coalesced packets that were triggering fragment reassembly in the IPsec layer. that reduced head-of-line blocking in lab but in one customer env it increased interrupts; so it's a tradeoff.
[03:10] Daniel Kwan: interrupts got pretty high on one of our 40g nics, cpu steal went up. we had to enable irqbalance. not sure if that's an acceptable tradeoff in prod.
[03:28] Miguel Alvarez: totally — that's why we want to run structured tests: one matrix varying MTU (1400/1420/1450), GRO on/off, and IPsec fragmentation settings. we'll surface p99, packet loss, and CPU impact.
[03:55] Priya Shah: what about kernel versions? your pilot node is on 5.15 right? our infra team is hesitant to move kernels mid-poc.
[04:10] Ruth Chen: current pilot image uses 5.15 LTS with some backported netstack patches. Miguel has a kernel tuning playbook that lists sysctl changes we recommend and the risk level. we'll share that.
[04:28] Miguel Alvarez: yep I'll drop the playbook. it includes net.core.rmem_max, net.ipv4.tcp_rmem, net.ipv4.tcp_low_latency toggles, and guidance for NIC offload flags. also notes for iptables conntrack and conntrack_max.
[04:50] Daniel Kwan: can you call out which changes are safe for non-disruptive hot reconfigure vs which require reboot? that's huge for our change windows.
[05:05] Miguel Alvarez: absolutely, there's a short list of sysctls that can be toggled live; I'll annotate. anything that touches the kernel module won't be live.
[05:18] Priya Shah: on the KV cache cold-start: is there a way to persist the cache across failovers or snapshot state? we saw a 400-600ms penalty on cold keys.
[05:34] Miguel Alvarez: persistence isn't safe across different runtime versions yet; what we've done for other pilots is prefix pre-warm during planned failover and increase the cache TTL to reduce churn. also we can use a warmup run after a new model load.
[05:52] Ruth Chen: note — there's also a quantization tradeoff: lower precision models have smaller KV state and faster loads but slightly different perf/quality. Miguel can put numbers in the playbook.
[06:12] Priya Shah: ok... the other weird thing we saw overnight was a spike correlated with a third-party CDN fail — meaning lead to traffic spikes to the private cluster. our autoscale handled throughput but p99 spiked.
[06:30] Daniel Kwan: yeah we saw a burst test where concurrent open connections hit 18k and we had connection churn. the service mesh sidecar was also rate limiting retries, which made tail worse.
[06:45] Miguel Alvarez: that's interesting — sidecars add headroom constraints. we generally recommend terminating TLS at the edge when possible and keep inter-node traffic plain for performance-critical paths, with link encryption at IPsec layer.
[07:05] Lina Morales: minor correction — we prefer MTLS for east-west to meet our policy, so can't fully drop sidecars. can we profile sidecar CPU usage?
[07:18] Miguel Alvarez: yes we can — we'll include sidecar profiling in the synthetic load runs.
[07:30] Ruth Chen: quick housekeeping: Rhe playbook and test matrix will be in the shared drive. also we'll propose a bakeoff window next Tuesday if that works for your change freeze.
[07:45] Priya Shah: Tuesday the 14th is fine, but blackout windows are 10:00-12:00 UTC for the billing batch.
[08:00] Daniel Kwan: ok keep it outside that.
[08:10] Miguel Alvarez: moving on — telemetry: we've seen sampling cadence at 1% may be missing important tails. we recommend adaptive sampling keyed to request latency and upstream error rates.
[08:28] Daniel Kwan: right now it's 1% globally and we have a few golden trace endpoints we'd like to force sample. can Redwood do deterministic golden trace capture?
[08:40] Miguel Alvarez: yes, we can tag golden traces by route and force-sample them; that'll give you full KV dump for those requests.
[08:55] Priya Shah: please do that for the top 5 user-facing routes. also we need GDPR redaction in traces, make sure PII isn't leaking in dump.
[09:08] Lina Morales: confirmed — redact at collection time; we can't give raw passenger data in logs.
[09:20] Miguel Alvarez: we'll redact on our side and also provide a whitebox guide for how to scrub traces.
[09:35] Ruth Chen: OK next — test results you sent: the nightly run on 2027-05-30 shows two distinct tail clusters, one correlating to fragmentation and another to KV cold-start on failover. any comment?
[09:55] Daniel Kwan: yes, the first cluster is 95-120ms additional latency during fragmented reassembly; the second cluster is 400-600ms after live node restart.
[10:10] Miguel Alvarez: that second cluster suggests cache misses and also slower model loader behaviour under IO contention. do you have IO wait traces?
[10:22] Daniel Kwan: we have iostat and top outputs — will upload. expect some IO spikes during model pulls to local SSD.
[10:30] Priya Shah: question — would switching to a compressed checkpoint image reduce load time? or will that just shift CPU to decompression?
[10:42] Miguel Alvarez: compressed checkpoints help network transfer but increase CPU on load; with our quantized artifacts the net win has been positive in many pilots but it's workload-dependent. we'll add a compressed vs uncompressed test.
[10:58] Ruth Chen: and we'll include the impact on cold start and model reload times in the matrix.
[11:10] Priya Shah: on security/compliance — Lina what else you need from Redwood to close the compliance gap?
[11:20] Lina Morales: we need proof of SOC2 scope for the private control plane, KMS integration steps, audit log retention guarantees, and a list of where encryption at rest happens. also a description of RBAC model and SSO integration options.
[11:38] Ruth Chen: got it — we'll push a compliance packet. Miguel, any blockers on that?
[11:44] Miguel Alvarez: none, but some of the on-prem packaging instructions assume an ops user with sudo; we'll document minimal privileges.
[11:54] Daniel Kwan: another small ask — can we get a pre-baked iptables set with conntrack tuned for high conn churn? we had conntrack storms.
[12:06] Miguel Alvarez: yes, that's standard; we'll provide a tuned set and caveats.
[12:18] Priya Shah: about the bakeoff: can you run a controlled failover where you simulate model reloads and ipsec tunnel bounce during non-billing hours and we observe tail?
[12:33] Miguel Alvarez: yes we can do that. plan: 3 runs — baseline, ipsec flapping, and node restart with pre-warm scripts. we'll capture p50/p95/p99, CPU, packet retransmit rates, and iostat.
[12:50] Ruth Chen: we'll also instrument to capture golden traces and KV cache hit ratio.
[13:00] Daniel Kwan: timeline wise when will you run the runs?
[13:05] Miguel Alvarez: aim to kick off fixtures on Friday 2027-06-11 and produce a results summary by Monday the 14th. but we can shift earlier if you want a midweek window.
[13:20] Priya Shah: Friday is ok as long as we avoid the 10-12 blackout.
[13:28] Ruth Chen: noted. Miguel will step through test matrix in a sec — can you quickly call out the matrix?
[13:35] Miguel Alvarez: matrix v1: MTU [1400, 1420, 1450], GRO [on/off], IPsec fragmentation [pfail/normal], sidecar [mtls on/off], model load [cold/warm], cache TTL [30/60/180]. we run 3 iterations each and capture the metrics.
[13:55] Daniel Kwan: sounds comprehensive, will that generate a lot of data? we need to ensure our storage doesn't overflow.
[14:03] Miguel Alvarez: we will cap trace retention and only keep aggregated metrics in the primary report; full pcap/traces for flagged runs only.
[14:15] Priya Shah: question on cost — Ruth, is there an expected delta if we change cache TTL or run more warmups? our budget is sensitive to token/unit costs.
[14:28] Ruth Chen: longer TTLs slightly increase memory usage but can reduce token costs by reducing recomputation. Miguel will quantify memory vs token cost tradeoff for a 100k req/day profile.
[14:42] Miguel Alvarez: yes I'll put a small model showing cost delta with TTL adjustments and quantization options.
[14:55] Lina Morales: one more security item: we need to verify that forced golden trace sampling doesn't replicate plaintext PII to Redwood logs. please ensure scrub rules run before export.
[15:10] Miguel Alvarez: agreed; scrub pipeline will run client-side hooks, we'll provide config for redaction patterns.
[15:23] Ruth Chen: ok near the end here — any blockers for the team?
[15:28] Priya Shah: main blocker is scheduling the bakeoff outside our billing blackout and verifying the compliance docs.
[15:36] Daniel Kwan: also need the packet captures from Redwood side correlated with our tcpdump; would help debugging.
[15:44] Miguel Alvarez: we'll share synchronized captures; timestamped.
[15:50] Ruth Chen: final recap: action items — Miguel runs synthetic MTU/IPsec tests and shares captures by 6/10; Daniel uploads p99 traces by 6/8; Ruth shares kernel playbook and cost delta by 6/9; Priya/Lina confirm compliance docs list by 6/11. bakeoff targeted for Fri 6/11 outside 10-12 UTC.
[16:20] Priya Shah: thanks all, that's clear.
[16:28] Lina Morales: thanks, we'll review the compliance packet when it's posted.
[16:35] Daniel Kwan: ok signing off, will upload traces tonight.
[16:42] Ruth Chen: thanks everyone, end 52 min.

End of transcript.
